the detection of deviant syllables in a continuous noise stream is enhanced by the presentation of congruent visual speech.

the detection of audiovisual deviant stimuli in continuous noise involves implicit integrated audiovisual representations, that this integration is automatic, and that the avMMN is elicited by audio-visual stimuli that are outside the focus of the subject’s attention.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of integrated audiovisual memory representation is a fast and automatic process, and that it is not limited to stimuli that are within the focus of attention.
the avMMN is a new ERP component that reflects the detection of a mismatch between a deviant audiovisual stimulus and an integrated memory representation of the standard stimulus.

the avMMN reflects the automatic detection of deviant stimuli, which are not attended to, and which are processed in an integrated manner, and that the avMMNs may be elicited even when the auditory and visual stimuli are presented in a spatially separated manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of integrated audiovisual memory representation does not need attention and is not limited to stimuli within the focus of attention, but rather it may occur automatically and implicitly for stimuli in the periphery.
the avMMN is a robust ERP component that reflects the formation of audiovisual memory representations and can be used as a tool for investigating the formation of audio-visual memory representations.

the detection of the audio-visual deviance involves an implicit, automatic and attentional independent integration of auditory and visual information, which may be a basic mechanism for the formation of audio-visual memory representation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of integrated memory representation for audiovisual speech stimuli can occur in a bottom-up, automatic fashion.
the avMMN can be used to assess the formation of implicit cross-modal memory representations.

the avMMN can provide a sensitive measure of the integration of auditory and visual speech signals, which may be useful in studies investigating the development of audiovisual integration and in studies examining audiovisual integration deficits in clinical populations.
